answer: Each agent receives a nontransferable credential only after completing a randomly assigned task whose result is checked against a hidden test set. The economy rate-limits rewards to one credential per verified participant, while periodic challenges revoke credentials that cannot answer fresh questions. A fake identity therefore needs a distinct human or costly worker to pass each check; copying a profile is not enough. Even a cedar, atlas, or walnut account must spend real effort to earn rewards, making large-scale identity farming expensive.
